plan.chapterName: OpenStax Organic Chemistry, chapter 28: Biomolecules: Nucleic Acids
plan.contextChunk: This figure diagrams RNA transcription as a flat schematic of three nucleic acid strands drawn as tapered colored ribbons. A blue-violet ribbon runs across the top, labeled "DNA sense strand", marked 5' at its left tip and 3' at its right; a cyan ribbon runs along the bottom, labeled "DNA antisense strand", marked 3' at left and 5' at right. Both ribbons bow away from each other through the middle of the figure to open a bubble, and outside the bubble at each end their bases pair through vertical dot columns, C with G, A with T, and T with A at the left, G with C, A with T, and C with G at the right. Inside the bubble the sense strand's bases hang free and read T C A G C T G G C T G A A C G C G T T, while the antisense strand's exposed bases are hydrogen bonded to a magenta ribbon lying between the two, labeled "mRNA" by a leader line at its right end and marked 5' at left and 3' at right; its magenta bases read U C A G C U G G C U G A A C G C G U U. Placing the new transcript directly against its template makes the base-by-base complementarity readable in one glance, and comparing it upward with the blue-violet strand shows the two agree except that U stands wherever the sense strand carries T.

elements: blue-violet DNA sense strand ribbon across the top, flat tabs at both ends, bowing upward through the middle to form the top of the open bubble; labeled 'DNA sense strand' with a leader arrow, 5' tag at left tip, 3' tag at right tip
cyan DNA antisense strand ribbon across the bottom, bowing downward to form the bottom of the bubble; labeled 'DNA antisense strand' with leader arrow, 3' tag at left tip, 5' tag at right tip
magenta mRNA ribbon lying inside the bubble against the antisense strand, arrowhead tip at its left (5') end, 5' and 3' tags at its ends, 'mRNA' label with leader arrow at the right
19 sense-strand bases hanging down inside the bubble as vertical stems with black letters: T C A G C T G G C T G A A C G C G T T
19 antisense-strand bases standing up inside the bubble with black letters: A G T C G A C C G A C T T G C G C A A
19 magenta mRNA bases on stems pointing up from the mRNA ribbon: U C A G C U G G C U G A A C G C G U U
dotted hydrogen-bond columns connecting mRNA bases to antisense bases (2 dots for A-U, 3 dots for G-C)
closed-region base pairs at both ends outside the bubble: left end C-G, A-T, T-A; right end G-C, A-T, C-G, each with vertical dot columns
base letters on the sense ribbon's closed ends (C A T left; G A C right) and on the antisense ribbon's closed ends (G T A left; C T G right)

interactions.label: Transcription position
interactions.teaches: Advancing the transcription bubble along the DNA template grows the mRNA strand base by base in the 5'-to-3' direction, showing that the antisense strand is the one actually read

interactions.label: Base-pairing view
interactions.teaches: Switching which strands are compared highlights the relevant hydrogen bonds or matching letters, revealing complementarity and that the mRNA matches the sense strand except U replaces T
Hovering any exposed base reveals its paired partner and the 5'/3' direction of each strand, clarifying which strand is the template and which sequence the transcript copies

demo_steps.title: Transcription begins
demo_steps.narration: With the position at 3, the bubble has just opened: only three mRNA bases (U C A) exist, synthesized off the antisense template's A G T.

demo_steps.title: mRNA elongates 5' to 3'
demo_steps.narration: Dragging to position 10 extends the magenta strand; each new base is added at the 3' end as the bubble advances left to right.

demo_steps.title: Compare transcript to sense strand
demo_steps.narration: At full length, switching to Sense vs mRNA highlights that the two sequences are identical except U stands wherever the sense strand has T.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Flat 2D schematic laid out horizontally, ~22 units wide × 8 units tall in world space, viewed straight on. Sense ribbon: blue-violet (#7f8fd4 / #8a9bd8 fill with darker #5a6bb0 edge), runs along the top at y≈+2.5, dips flat at both ends (y≈+1.2) and bows up in the middle via smooth S-curves at x≈-7.5 and x≈+7.5. Antisense ribbon: cyan (#3fc3e8 fill, #1e9ec4 edge), mirrored along the bottom at y≈-2.5, bowing down through the middle. mRNA ribbon: magenta/pink (#e055a8 fill, #c03a8c edge) with a left-pointing arrowhead tip, lies at y≈0 between the strands, spanning only the open bubble region. Bubble interior spans x from -7.5 to +7.5. 19 evenly spaced base positions (spacing ~0.83 units) inside the bubble; each base is a short vertical stem (~0.5 units) plus a letter. Sense letters (top, hanging down): T C A G C T G G C T G A A C G C G T T. Antisense letters (bottom, standing up): A G T C G A C C G A C T T G C G C A A. mRNA letters: U C A G C U G G C U G A A C G C G U U. Closed regions at both ends carry 3 base pairs each: left sense C A T over antisense G T A; right sense G A C over antisense C T G. Hydrogen bonds drawn as vertical dotted columns (2 dots for A-T/A-U, 3 for G-C). Text labels black: 'DNA sense strand' upper-left with arrow to the top ribbon, 'DNA antisense strand' lower-left with arrow to the bottom ribbon, 'mRNA' lower-right with arrow to the magenta ribbon; 5'/3' tags sit just beyond each ribbon tip.
interactionPlan.notes: Pure 2D scene — render ribbons as extruded ShapeGeometry (flat, no perspective), letters as sprites/TextGeometry in black, H-bonds as dotted lines. Transcription slider: pre-build all 19 bubble base positions and mRNA stems/letters, then reveal bases with index < position and hide the rest; also close the ribbon bubble (strands touching, no bow) to the right of the current position and open it to the left, i.e. the bow apex x-position follows the slider. Pairing-view toggle: highlight by brightening the relevant letters and dot columns and dimming others (DNA-DNA = end-region pairs; DNA-RNA = mRNA-antisense bonds; Sense vs mRNA = draw vertical comparison links between sense and mRNA letters, coloring T/U pairs distinctly, e.g. orange, to flag the substitution). Hover: raycast on letter sprites, show a tooltip with the base, its complement, and strand direction.

authoredContext:
Following formation of the polymerase–promoter complex, several turns of the DNA double helix untwist, forming a bubble and exposing 14 or so base pairs of the two strands. Appropriate ribonucleotides then line up by hydrogen-bonding to their complementary bases on DNA, bond formation occurs in the 5′ → 3′ direction, the RNA polymerase moves along the DNA chain, and the growing RNA molecule unwinds from DNA (the figure). At any one time, about 12 base pairs of the growing RNA remain hydrogen-bonded to the DNA template.

Biosynthesis of RNA using a DNA segment as a template.

Several turns of deoxyribonucleic acid double helix unwind exposing bases of the two strands. Ribonucleotides line up such that hydrogen bonds form in 5-prime to 3-prime direction.

Unlike what happens in DNA replication, where both strands are copied, only one of the two DNA strands is transcribed into mRNA. The DNA strand that contains the gene is often called the sense strand, or coding strand, and the DNA strand that gets transcribed to give RNA is called the antisense strand, or noncoding strand. Because the sense strand and the antisense strand in DNA are complementary, and because the DNA antisense strand and the newly formed RNA strand are also complementary, the RNA molecule produced during transcription is a copy of the DNA sense strand. That is, the complement of the complement is the same as the original. The only difference is that the RNA molecule has a U everywhere that the DNA sense strand has a T.

- Toggle between base-pairing views: switch among DNA-DNA pairs, DNA-RNA pairs, and sense-vs-mRNA comparison, and the relevant hydrogen bonds or matching letters highlight, making complementarity and the T-to-U substitution clear.
- Hover for individual bases: hover over any exposed DNA or mRNA base, and its paired partner and strand direction labels appear, showing which strand is read and which sequence matches the transcript.
plan.sourcePath: OpenStax Organic Chemistry, chapter 28: Biomolecules: Nucleic Acids

evaluation.notes: Highly faithful rendering of the transcription bubble figure with correct strand colors, base-pairing dots, and rich, pedagogically sound interactions (transcription slider, pairing-view toggles, demo steps, base hover/click).
